entry.title: [NEW] GO-2026-6866: Check all ancestor namespace transitions when rendering raw text in html in golang.org/x/net
entry.content:
Check all ancestor namespace transitions when rendering raw text in html in golang.org/x/net

Aliases: CVE-2026-97045

Affected:

  • golang.org/x/net — fixed in 0.62.0

In childTextNodesAreLiteral, walking up the tree previously stopped at the nearest foreign ancestor once an HTML integration point was found. However, that integration point may itself be a descendant of an element that was foster-parented into a foreign namespace (such as <mglyph> or <malignmark> fostered under <mtext>), causing a parser to resolve the subtree in a different foreign namespace upon re-parsing the rendered output. Continue walking the full ancestor chain and verify that every transition from a non-empty namespace occurs at an HTML integration point before emitting literal text.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/855121
  • https://go.dev/issue/82622
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/sqrs2vTx_Xs

entry.title: [NEW] GO-2026-6860: Avoid quadratic complexity when coalescing text nodes in html in golang.org/x/net
entry.content:
Avoid quadratic complexity when coalescing text nodes in html in golang.org/x/net

Aliases: CVE-2026-78661

Affected:

  • golang.org/x/net — fixed in 0.62.0

When coalescing adjacent text nodes in addText and fosterParent, appending to an existing TextNode's Data via string concatenation (n.Data += text) reallocated and copied the accumulated string on every token. Inputs containing many short text runs separated by ignored end tags (such as "a</x>") caused O(n^2) allocations and byte copies. Accumulate coalesced text in per-node byte slices during parsing and materialize Data strings once at the end of parse.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/849365
  • https://go.dev/issue/82224
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/sqrs2vTx_Xs

Aliases: CVE-2026-116682

Affected:

  • github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/backend — fixed in 0.0.0-20260814233832-4126edeb07a0

## Summary File read paths resolve symbolic links with `filepath.EvalSymlinks` and then operate on the resolved target without re-checking that the target still lies inside the user's source/scope. Any authenticated user with download access can read files anywhere the server process can, whenever such a symlink is reachable in their scope. entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-vg84-c5mg-76xh: CTFer.io's CTFd Terraform Provider allows a local or remote attacker to read team passwords in state as non sensitive values
entry.content:
CTFer.io's CTFd Terraform Provider allows a local or remote attacker to read team passwords in state as non sensitive values

Aliases: CVE-2026-116683

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:L/SA:N

Affected:

  • github.com/ctfer-io/terraform-provider-ctfd
  • github.com/ctfer-io/terraform-provider-ctfd/v2 — fixed in 2.8.2

### Impact CTFer.io's CTFd Terraform Provider stores `ctfd_team.password` as non-sensitive values (CWE-522). A local or remote attacker, who can have access to the Terraform state, can read team passwords without the need for the state password for decryption. ### Patches Patched in v2.8.2. ### Workarounds No workaround exist, yet CTFer.io recommends you keep your state in safe environments with a limited set of users who can access it as a good practice to avoid exploitation of this vulnerability.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-4hv6-xc92-j86g: Vikunja: WebSocket authentication ignores server-side session state, so revoked sessions keep receiving live pushes
entry.content:
Vikunja: WebSocket authentication ignores server-side session state, so revoked sessions keep receiving live pushes

Aliases: CVE-2026-111917, GO-2026-6715

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • code.vikunja.io/api — fixed in 2.7.0

### Summary Vikunja v2.6.0 introduced server-side sessions with revocation semantics: `DELETE /api/v2/user/sessions/{id}` documents "Revokes a specific session by its UUID", and enabling TOTP calls `DeleteAllUserSessions` to invalidate all sessions. The WebSocket endpoint accepts any cryptographically valid user JWT without ever resolving its `sid` (session id) claim against the sessions table. A connection authenticated before revocation stays authenticated and continues to receive live pushes indefinitely, and even brand-new WebSocket connections are accepted with a token whose session was deleted. The revocation feature therefore does not cover the WebSocket boundary at all. ### Details User access JWTs carry a session reference: `NewUserJWTAuthtoken` (`pkg/modules/auth/auth.go:188`)…

Affected:

## Summary Vikunja's `web.Auth` interface (`pkg/web/web.go`, single method `GetID() int64`) is satisfied by BOTH `*user.User` and `*models.LinkSharing`. A link-share's `GetID()` returns the **raw positive** `share.ID` (`pkg/models/link_sharing.go:83-85`), which lives in the same positive autoincrement ID space as `users.id`. As a result, a link-share principal with id `N` — which should have zero authority over teams or bot users — is treated as the *user* whose `users.id == N` at three permission checks that lack the `a.(*LinkSharing)` guard their sibling methods have. ### Summary In Vikunja v2.6.0 the task position recalculation that runs when a saved filter view is created fails open when the requesting user has no accessible projects.
